title: Terraform module: OTLP + Fluent Bit retention & graceful drain hooks for VPC observability
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce lifecycle and upgrade safety features to the existing Terraform module that provisions the VPC observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry Collector). This ticket expands the module to add: 1) configurable log retention and S3 cold-storage lifecycle hooks for shipped logs, 2) a lightweight Fluent Bit daemonset option for constrained VPCs that cannot run Vector, 3) Terraform-driven graceful drain & rolling-upgrade hooks (null_resources + local-exec) to coordinate KV cache flushes and collector bump rollouts, 4) an automated canary healthcheck job (k8s CronJob) that validates end-to-end scraping, ingestion, and query surface after changes, and 5) migration helpers for existing clusters to opt into the new retention/cold-storage model without data loss. Goals: reduce upgrade blips during collector/prometheus rollouts, improve cost control via retention lifecycle rules, and provide a deterministic rollback path for failed upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes retention_days and s3_lifecycle_policy variables and applies without destroying existing indices
Optional Fluent Bit daemonset can be enabled via fluentbit_enabled=true and is deployable in air-gapped VPCs
A null_resource-based drain hook runs pre-upgrade to flush OTLP/KV caches and waits for /health to return OK before proceeding
Canary CronJob runs a synthetic scrape->ingest->query flow; failure rate >0 triggers rollback plan and Slack alert
Upgrade runbook documented with step-by-step commands and automated checks in the module README
design_decisions: Choose Fluent Bit for log shipping in constrained environments: lower memory footprint and mature S3 plugins compared to Vector
Implement retention as S3 lifecycle rules for raw logs and use Prometheus remote_write retention only for metrics; avoids expensive long-term storage in TSDB
Use Terraform null_resource + local-exec with exponential backoff for pre/post hooks instead of adding a separate operator to keep IaC-focused deploys
Canary healthcheck implemented as a Kubernetes CronJob to run inside customer VPCs so queries traverse the exact network path used in production
tradeoffs: Fluent Bit sacrifices some advanced filtering features present in Vector; acceptable for most private deployments to reduce resource consumption
Null_resource hooks rely on controller nodes having kubectl/helm access during apply; this increases operational coupling but keeps complexity out of the module
Using S3 lifecycle reduces storage cost but increases egress/read latency for long tail investigations; docs will include guidance and quick-restore steps

notes: Keep Terraform updates backwards compatible: avoid schema changes that force resource replacement for existing prometheus/grafana deployments.
We will provide a migration script (kubectl job) for customers with on-disk wal/indices to export to S3 before lifecycle policy takes effect.
Ops checklist: pre-upgrade snapshot, disable autoscaler for collector statefulsets, run canary, perform rolling upgrade, re-enable autoscaler
